description: Home-turf context-bench task corpus (docs/plans/home-bench.md H1-1) — the mirror of testdata/contextbench/tasks.json's grep-native B1 corpus. Where B1 measured grep's home turf (governance/enforcement questions are absent by construction there — see B1's corpus-mix disclosure in docs/plans/falsifiability.md), this corpus measures fathom's: obligations, verify, blast-radius, claim-provenance, concern-scoped search, contradiction, and staleness. Every ground_truth here was independently hand-verified against the fathom repo's actual files at the commit noted in each task's `source` field (never derived from the live daemon's opinion alone, per the plan's fairness rule 1) — most tasks additionally cite what the live daemon's obligations/blast-radius/call-hierarchy tools returned during authoring, purely as reconnaissance, with the hand-verification recorded alongside. See `pre_registered_criterion` (H2-1), `post_recompile_rederivation` (mandatory pre-H3 step), and `unmeasurable_by_comparison` (the fairness-rule-3 capabilities deliberately excluded from scoring).

pre_registered_criterion.source_of_registration: docs/plans/home-bench.md design section (H2 pre-registration), committed in git before this corpus file's first results run — git history ordering IS the registration evidence, not this JSON block alone.
pre_registered_criterion.criterion: fathom wins home turf only if BOTH hold: (1) the fathom arm's success count across this corpus is STRICTLY GREATER than the grep arm's (equal-or-worse success = refuted, per the plan's design section); AND (2) the fathom arm's total tokens are <= 1x the grep arm's total tokens (no token premium for winning — unlike B1, which retracted at <5x reduction, home-turf's bar is tighter: even token PARITY is acceptable, a token premium is not).
pre_registered_criterion.verdict_recording: H3-1 (op-gated, docs/plans/home-bench.md) records the run's results artifact + verdict, honest either way, once run.
pre_registered_criterion.caveats_carried_from_b1: n=1 corpus, single machine, dollar-cost not pre-registered as a criterion (recorded for context only, per B1-3's precedent).

machine_criterion.description: fathom wins home turf only if BOTH hold: strictly more successes than grep, AND aggregate tokens <= 1x grep's. Machine-evaluable form of pre_registered_criterion.criterion, evaluated by internal/contextbench.Criterion.Evaluate — the only thing permitted to declare a win.
machine_criterion.min_trials_registered: 2026-09-01: a replication floor NOT present in the original H2-1 registration. The 2026-07-24 and T5-8 runs were n=1 per cell and are therefore indeterminate under this criterion, not retroactively invalidated — their recorded verdicts stand as accurate history of an n=1 instrument. The floor binds every run from its registration commit forward.

leak_rule.registered: 2026-09-02 (PB-9, ADR-031 §3), before any run with a `none` arm. A third arm with every tool disallowed and no MCP servers measures the memorisation floor; a task it passes in >= 2 of 3 trials is `leaked` (internal/contextbench.LeakedTasks), excluded from the verdict, and listed in the ledger row's leaked_tasks so the exclusion is visible. Excluding a leaked task never softens the bar: it removes a task neither arm needed tools for. Revisit (ADR-031): if the none arm passes more than half the corpus, the corpus — not the tool — is the finding.

registered_criteria.description: Precision-aware form of H2-1 (PB-8, ADR-031 §3; docs/vision/26-proof-credibility.md §2.2). Same bar — strictly more successes than grep, aggregate tokens <= 1x, replication floor 3 — but a cell SUCCEEDS only when the arm's answer is a fenced ``` block whose non-empty lines number at most the task's max_predicted (default max(5, 2·|gold|)) and whose text satisfies the task's scoring rule; test-file paths are dropped from gold. Scored by internal/contextbench.ScoreWithPrecision; precision and recall are recorded beside pass/fail in every ArmResult and reported, never gating. Registered as a NEW criterion because it changes the success definition after H2-1 has recorded data: H2-1's verdicts (2026-07-24, T5-8, the backfilled ledger row) stand as history and are never re-scored under H2-2 (T5).

The criterion the next full run is scored on (BP-10, ADR-032 §3; docs/design/bench-pyramid.md §3.5). SAME success bar as H2-1 — strictly more successes than the control arm, replication floor 3, substring scoring, the same committed leak rule. DIFFERENT cost half: `payload_bytes` (the sum of tool-result bytes returned to the model, internal/contextbench.TranscriptMetrics) ratio <= 1.0 AND `cost_usd` ratio <= 1.0. total_tokens is RECORDED and NOT gated: the first replicated run showed it to be cache_read x turns — a turn counter in a token costume, under which the discovery payload fathom shrinks is invisible (O26). `toolsearch_turns` (the harness's deferred MCP schema loads, O24) is reported as its own line per arm and never gated: it is a harness tax, so it may not penalise the fathom arm silently, and naming it stops it being an excuse either. `gold_source_tool` — the tool whose result first carried a gold token — is recorded per cell and summarised as gold_source_rate per arm per tool on the ledger row, so a tool passes only when it is the source (E1/O23: obligations served six displaced rules and the arm passed the task anyway by reading the file grep's way). Registered as a NEW criterion because it changes the cost half after H2-1 recorded data; H2-1's verdicts stand as history and are never re-scored (T5). Evaluated by internal/contextbench.Criterion.Evaluate; a run that recorded no payload_bytes is INDETERMINATE under it, never a pass — the instrument did not look.

Grep COULD in principle enumerate every function name repo-wide and diff signatures pairwise, but at repo scale this is not a task any human or agent arm can complete inside a bench turn budget — a real path in theory, not in practice, so excluded from scoring rather than padding either arm's number.
